stem: After a justified micronutrient correction, new growth improves while previously damaged leaves remain visibly affected. How should the response be evaluated?
choices: Use new growth and repeated trend measurements; old damaged tissue may not fully recover even when the underlying issue improves.
Treat the correction as incomplete because previously damaged leaves should return close to normal if the diagnosis was correct.
Increase the correction again because persistent symptoms on old leaves indicate the original adjustment was too small.
Weight the old leaves more heavily than new growth because established tissue provides a longer record of nutrient status.
rationale: Recovery is often best judged from new growth and trends. Existing tissue damage may be irreversible and should not be the sole success criterion.
